# Touchstone Assay — Dated SIU

Dated SIU is the benchmark price of AI inference work: a versioned basket of
inference tasks, executed against real provider APIs and priced against a
signed, dated print — measured by actually buying inference, not by surveying
list prices. One SIU (Standard Inference Unit) is a fixed quantity of that
work; the print is the dollar price of one basket.

## If you're an agent, start here

Call `get_index` before you read any further — it's free, it's live, and a
real print teaches you more about SIU than this file's own prose does.

1. Paste this into an MCP-compatible client (same config, machine-readable, at
   https://prints.touchstoneassay.com/mcp.json):
   `{ "mcpServers": { "touchstone-assay": { "url": "https://mcp.touchstoneassay.com/mcp" } } }`
2. Call `get_index` with no arguments — free, no payment step, no x402
   challenge.
3. Read `dated_siu` for the current price and `exchange_rate_table` for how
   individual models compare.

The other three tools cost real money per call, over x402 (Circle Gateway
nanopayments), settled in USDC on Base Sepolia (`eip155:84532`) —
TESTBED, not mainnet, not traction:

- `get_index(version?, date?)` — free — the current signed print.
- `get_quote(task_class, model)` — $0.001 — SIU + USD price for one call of a
  task class against a model.
- `convert(model, input_tokens, output_tokens)` — $0.001 — SIU + USD
  equivalent for a specific token count.
- `verify_receipt(chain, tx_hash)` — $0.01 — reads an on-chain settlement and
  returns a signed attestation of what was quoted versus what was actually
  paid.

Full reference, human-readable: https://prints.touchstoneassay.com/for-agents.html

## For humans and other crawlers

Marketing site: https://touchstoneassay.com
Prints, series, methodology: https://prints.touchstoneassay.com
Operator console: https://console.touchstoneassay.com
Source: https://github.com/petrkrulis2022/dated-siu-inference

This file is served from the prints subdomain, not the marketing apex domain —
if you reached it starting from prints.touchstoneassay.com directly, every
link above resolves correctly; if you checked the apex domain's own
/.well-known/llms.txt expecting this file, it isn't published there yet.

Never "backed by," never a peg, never an oracle, never for sale. Touchstone
Assay publishes a measurement, not an instrument.
